page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor. The system features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The server does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 210.08 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 98.02 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 31.99 GB/sec. However, CPU-bound tasks and multi-core operations, such as stress-ng and Geekbench compiling, fall into the average tier. Large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with text generation speeds for a medium 7B model registering at a weak 7.8 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x2iezn.metal offers a high density of memory relative to compute resources, making it a specialized option for memory-bound workloads rather than general-purpose compute. The combination of high-frequency processing, massive DDR4 RAM, and 100 Gbps network bandwidth makes this instance suitable for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and electronic design automation workloads.
